tasks.spec:
You are an implementation worker REDESIGNING a checker whose primary signal was proven miscalibrated on real media. Copy /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/one-true-master/checks/resolution_check.py into your current working directory as ./resolution_check.py and rework it in place. READ access to /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast; never write to it. Pure stdlib + numpy + ffmpeg/ffprobe subprocess. No git, no MCP, no network.

WHAT IT MUST PROVE: a finished video master carries the picture resolution its cameras actually captured — catching a pipeline that silently downscaled intermediates (real defect: every speaker stem hard-coded to 960x540 while cameras shot 1920x1080 and 1280x720, then upscaled back to a 1080p master).

MEASURED EVIDENCE (all from the real episode; use these numbers to calibrate):
1. The UPSCALE_FINGERPRINT check (halve-and-restore detail retention, absolute threshold <= 0.92) is INVALID for this content class. The RAW camera file itself scores retention 1.000-1.008 — video-conference webcam footage is natively soft, so it has no fine detail to lose at 1080p even straight from the camera. Absolute sharpness cannot distinguish "upscaled" from "genuinely soft source". It produced a FALSE RED on a correctly-rendered HD composite.
2. Cross-artifact DETAIL DISTRIBUTION comparison is also invalid as used, because the artifacts have different FRAMING: the composite is side-by-side (each speaker at half width) while the final is angle-switched full-frame. Comparing their detail distributions gave a backwards verdict (old bad master 0.990, new good composite 0.947).
3. A CONTROLLED experiment on identical source frames is decisive: pushing the same raw frames through the old path (scale to 960x540 then back to 1920x1080) keeps 86.5% of source detail; the new path (stay at 1920x1080) keeps 100.0%. So a genuine downscale round-trip costs about 13-14% of detail on this content — but this is only measurable when comparing the SAME framing of the SAME content.

THE REDESIGN — lead with the deterministic structural check, keep signal checks as same-framing comparisons only:
1. STEM_RESOLUTION (new, PRIMARY, deterministic): accept --stems DIR (directory of per-speaker video stems) and --sources PATH... (raw camera tracks). ffprobe each. FAIL when any stem's width or height is BELOW min(that stem's best-matching source dimension, the delivery canvas from --canvas WxH default 1920x1080). Match stems to sources by index order after sorting both, and say in the output which stem was compared to which source, so a mismatch is visible rather than silent. This check alone catches the real defect exactly, with no thresholds and no content sensitivity — it is the gate's backbone. When --stems is not supplied, report STEM_RESOLUTION as SKIPPED with a WHY (never silently pass).
2. DECLARED_RESOLUTION (keep as-is): final dimensions must not be below the source envelope.
3. SAME_FRAMING_DETAIL (replaces the cross-artifact distribution check): compare the FINAL only against its DIRECT same-framing ancestor supplied as --ancestor PATH (the angle-switched program, which shares the final's full-frame framing). Sample --probe-count aligned timestamps: the final = head_offset + ancestor time, with --head-offset-s (default 0.0) supplied by the caller for the intro bumper. Compute the median detail ratio final/ancestor and FAIL below --min-detail-ratio (default 0.85, since a same-framing re-encode should retain nearly everything and a 960->1920 round trip costs ~13.5%). When --ancestor is absent, report SKIPPED with a WHY.
4. DELETE the absolute UPSCALE_FINGERPRINT check, or demote it to an INFO line that reports retention for both the final AND every source and explicitly states it is advisory, never a FAIL. Document in a comment WHY it cannot gate: measured raw-camera retention 1.000-1.008 on real footage.
Keep the durationless-WebM packet-timestamp duration fallback and the exit-2-on-unusable-input behavior exactly as they are.

SELF-TEST (--self-test, hermetic, ffmpeg lavfi; keep every still-relevant existing case, and PRINT measured numbers for all): (a) stems at 1920x1080 with 1920x1080 sources PASS STEM_RESOLUTION; (b) RED: stems at 960x540 with 1920x1080 sources FAIL STEM_RESOLUTION and exit 1 — this is the exact shipped defect and it MUST be caught structurally; (c) a 1280x720 source with a 1920x1080 stem PASSES (upscaling a smaller camera onto the canvas is legitimate); (d) SAME_FRAMING_DETAIL passes when final and ancestor are the same content re-encoded, and RED: fails when the final is the ancestor round-tripped through 960x540; (e) a SOFT-SOURCE case proving the false red is gone: build a deliberately soft/blurred 1920x1080 source and a correct 1920x1080 final from it, and assert the overall verdict is PASS exit 0 (under the old absolute fingerprint this returned a false FAIL); (f) unusable input still exits 2. Self-test exits 0 only when every green case is green and every red case is red.
tasks.check: python3 '/mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/one-true-master/checks/script_check.py' resolution_check.py argparse '2026-06-10,fred-cho' && timeout 900 python3 resolution_check.py --self-test && echo PASS
tasks.verified: resolution gate leads with a deterministic stem-vs-source dimension check; no absolute-sharpness gating that false-reds soft webcam footage
